deals.body:
Only price reductions are promos (percent off, multi-buy, coupon, price below the regular price). Shipping fees, minimum orders and pack options go in the note, never in the promo label. A promo is a price with an end date: record it, watch it, and drop it when it ends.
- Store on every promo price: promo (label), promo_until (YYYY-MM-DD), regular_unit_price (the normal shelf price per unit), requires_program (loyalty program id, if a card or app is needed).
- If promo_until is in the past, the app ranks the item at regular_unit_price. With no regular price the row leaves the ranking and shows Promo ended until re-checked.
deals.title: Deals and promo expiry

health.body:
Reference nutrition per 100 g comes from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy) and is generic, not the retail pack label.
A cheaper product with added sugar or heavy processing is shown but never ranked best for health.
health.title: Health rubric

loyalty.body:
Use only free programs that match what is actually bought. Paid programs must save more than they cost.
Sample programs: Fresh Mart Club (AUR), Northgate Points (BOR), MegaMart Club (CAS, membership).
loyalty.title: Loyalty programs and cards

principles.body:
Value = price per kg / l / piece in EUR, after checking a promo has not expired. Pack price is never the comparison.
Comparison unit follows how the item is bought: weight (per kg), liquids (per l), counted things (per piece).
Health first: a cheaper product with added sugar or heavy processing is shown, but never ranked best for health.
Daily drivers are tracked tightly; one-off purchases only when cheap to check.
Stale data is not a price: older than 90 days, or an ended promo, counts as unknown until re-checked.
Only price reductions are promos. Shipping, minimum orders and pack options go in the note.
Prices are append-only: a changed price is a new row; an unchanged price only gets a new checked date.
Every price has an origin (yours or auto) and a source.
principles.title: Buying principles

sources.body: Prefer shop websites and flyers, then open price surveys, then photos of shelf tags. Record the source URL and date on every price. Sample data only: these shops and prices are invented.
sources.title: Where to fetch prices (sources playbook)
